body:
AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'sweep-adopt-veridian-scripts-422-fix-worker-stop-systemic-2s-worker-fast' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  pm_lifecycle.py              | 77 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++----
 superboss-register.py        | 10 ++++++
 worker-exit-status-bridge.py | 16 ++++++++-
 3 files changed, 96 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
Evidence Recorded: The diff correctly fixes the root-cause tier bug (default complexity_tier="moderate" was never a member of tight_task_validation.VALID_TIERS = [mechanical, integrative, judgment], causing every worker on that path to hit preflight-guard.py's hard stop ~2s in) and the superboss-register.py/worker-exit-status-bridge.py logs_ref wiring is sound (real column, parameterized write, subprocess called with an argv list so no shell-injection risk, best-effort/non-blocking). However, wiring build_tightened_prompt() to call validate_tight_task() at construction time introduces a second, newly-surfaced defect that breaks the two real callers this diff itself edited: I ran dispatch_audit_fix()'s and dispatch_independent_audit()'s exact, unmodified success_criteria strings through the actual validate_tight_task()/check_success_criteria_has_runnable_command() and both now unconditionally raise ValueError ("no_runnable_verification_command_in_success_criteria") because their command text (e.g. "gh pr view ... --comments -- then fix the real cited issue. Verify with: git -C . log -1 --format=%H") is embedded mid-sentence rather than on its own line starting with a recognized command word, so _line_is_runnable_command() never matches. verify_with_retries() calls dispatch_fix_fn/dispatch_audit_fn with no try/except around them, so this ValueError now propagates uncaught out of the audit-fail-retry loop and is only caught by main()'s top-level handler, aborting the entire run_full_cycle report with a bare internal_error instead of the real, partial report -- worse than the pre-fix behavior for these two paths (a real dispatch attempt that at least produced a pollable umr row). There is no test_pm_lifecycle.py exercising build_tightened_prompt/dispatch_audit_fix/dispatch_independent_audit, which is how this shipped without being caught. Diff does not touch .github/workflows/**, migrations, schema, auth, or secrets, so tier1 classification is not in question, but the regression is real and reproducible, not speculative. Issues found: dispatch_audit_fix() and dispatch_independent_audit() in pm_lifecycle.py now unconditionally raise ValueError from build_tightened_prompt()'s new validate_tight_task() call, because their real success_criteria text embeds the verification command mid-sentence instead of as its own recognized command line -- confirmed by executing the actual functions' real argument strings against the actual validator, not a hypothetical.; verify_with_retries() has no try/except around dispatch_fix_fn/dispatch_audit_fn, so this ValueError propagates out of the retry loop and is only caught by main()'s generic top-level handler, discarding the run's real partial report instead of failing gracefully or being caught per-dispatch like other outcomes (refused/rejected/unknown) are.; No unit test exists (no test_pm_lifecycle.py) exercising build_tightened_prompt(), dispatch_audit_fix(), or dispatch_independent_audit() with real argument text, which is why this regression was not caught before merge.; Minor: CLI default --complexity-tier changed to "integrative", which validate_tight_task() requires known_context for; any `pm_lifecycle.py run` invocation that omits --known-context now fails fast with a ValueError (confirmed) instead of dispatching -- likely an intentional fail-fast tradeoff but worth confirming it doesn't regress any existing caller that relied on omitting both flags for a mechanical-style task.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.
